newsitem.title: TURKEY: INTERVIEW-Turkish Beko to double sales.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Turkish Beko to double sales.

text.p: Leading Turkish electronic goods producer Beko Elektronik A.S., a unit of the industrial Koc conglomerate wants to double its sales in 1997, from an expected 20 trillion lira in 1996, a senior company official said.

"It will be easy for us to meet this target, because we have an order of 500,000 (television) units by Milliyet daily for its promotion campaign," Aydin Cubukcu, general manager of the company, told Reuters.
He said they would exceed 100 percent capacity utilisation by working on all holidays to realise the planned production of 1.3 million TV sets next year.
"And we will also increase our exports to $68 million in 1997 against $40-45 million in 1996, which will help us to raise the turnover by 100 percent," he said.
Beko shares closed at 10,500 lira on Wednesday, up from 9,900 lira on Tuesday.

The company reported provisional net profits of 1.85 trillion lira and net sales of 13.39 trillion lira in the first nine months of 1996, up sharply from 804.8 billion and 6.74 trillion lira respectively in the same 1995 period.

"We used to export more than 30 percent of our output until two of our top managers were transferred to Vestel Elektronik after which they passed us by gaining easy access to information on our export markets and customers," Cubukcu said.

The top managers were not anymore with Vestel, Cubukcu said, adding that Beko would in 1997 try to win back its export customers lost this year, by competitive pricing and expanding the product range.
Koc exports all durables produced within the group, including dish washers, refrigerators and TV sets, under Beko brand, to various European countries and Russia.

"Now our share in the UK TV sets market is four percent and over one percent in Germany," Cubukcu said. "But we also produce TV sets under 120 brands for foreign buyers, to increase our capacity utilisation."
Beko has an annual TV set production capacity of around 1,000,000 and had a capacity utilisation of around 70 percent with 670,000 units in 1996.
"We want to go on producing around 1.3 million sets after 1997. We will make a $10 million investment in 1997 to meet this target and continue to invest afterwards," Cubukcu said.
As one of the six domestic producers, Beko increased its market share in the Turkish TV set market to 39.1 percent in 1996 from 37.4 percent last year.
The company plans to launch a new high-tech TV set with normal and cinemascope dimensions in late 1997.
Beko also imports video and audio equipment from various producers and markets them in the domestic market.

"Even some newspapers give music sets against coupons as a result of the stiff promotion competition in the media. Demand for music sets is very strong," Cubukcu said. "We were the first to launch digital audio equipment to the Turkish market and we still maintain last year's 75.7 share."
He said Beko held a 93.4 percent share in videos and 55.1 percent share in cash tills.
Cubukcu complained about the European Union (EU) countries' "artificial" anti-dumping investigations.
Cubukcu said, the customs union could not badly affect Beko's domestic market share because foreign producers could only sell sophisticated, high-tech TV sets in the Turkish market, as Sony does.
Beko produces all parts of a TV set, apart from certain components like tubes and integrated circuits.
Cubukcu said they were also importing micro-controllers for the TV sets from the major worldwide producers like Motorola, Philips, Siemens and Panasonic.
"We design what we need and they produce it for us. An integrated circuit investment is not feasible in Turkey now, but I believe that it may realised in the future."
